text: The anti-discrimination measure refiled in the Senate in July 2025 for the 20th Congress is known as the SOGIESC Equality Bill. What does SOGIESC stand for?
optionA: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity or Expression, and Sex Characteristics
optionB: Social Orientation, Gender Inclusion and Equal Social Care
optionC: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Equality and Social Conduct
optionD: Sex, Orientation, Gender Inclusion, Equity and Social Citizenship
explanation: As of November 2026, the bill refiled in the 20th Congress covers discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC). The older name 'SOGIE' covers only the first three; 'SC' (sex characteristics) was added in later versions (GMA News, July 2025).
hint: The last two letters refer to physical traits a person is born with.
whyB: There is no 'social orientation' or 'social care' in the acronym. The 'SO' is sexual orientation.
whyC: The 'E' stands for expression, not equality, and 'SC' is not social conduct.
whyD: This splits the letters wrongly. SO is one term (sexual orientation) and GIE is gender identity or expression.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang SOGIESC ay Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity or Expression, and Sex Characteristics. Ito ang saklaw ng anti-discrimination bill na ni-refile sa 20th Congress noong July 2025 (GMA News). Yung 'SC' ang dinagdag sa mas lumang tawag na 'SOGIE'.
hintTl: Yung huling dalawang letra, tungkol sa physical traits na meron ka na pagkapanganak.

text: As of November 2026, which statement best describes the status of the SOGIE (SOGIESC) Equality Bill?
optionA: It was signed into law in 2024 as the SOGIESC Equality Act.
optionB: It was refiled in the 20th Congress and has not yet been enacted into law.
optionC: It was vetoed by the President after both chambers approved it in 2025.
optionD: It was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2023.
explanation: As of November 2026, the SOGIESC Equality Bill remains a pending measure: it was refiled in the Senate in July 2025 for the 20th Congress, and in July 2026 lawmakers were still urging its passage. It has been refiled in every Congress since it was first introduced in 2000 (GMA News, July 2025; Daily Tribune, July 2026).
hint: The bill has been refiled again and again across many Congresses.
whyA: No SOGIESC Equality Act has been enacted. The bill is still pending in Congress.
whyC: Both chambers have never approved the same version, so it never reached the President for signature or veto.
whyD: The Supreme Court can only rule on laws or acts, not on bills that have not been enacted.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, pending pa rin ang SOGIESC Equality Bill: ni-refile ito sa Senado noong July 2025 para sa 20th Congress, at noong July 2026 ay hinihimok pa rin ng mga mambabatas na maipasa ito. Ni-refile na ito sa bawat Congress mula nang unang i-file noong 2000 (GMA News; Daily Tribune).
hintTl: Paulit-ulit itong ni-re-refile sa bawat bagong Congress.

text: On September 20, 2017, the House of Representatives approved the SOGIE Equality Bill (House Bill 4982) on third and final reading. What happened to that measure afterward?
optionA: It was signed into law within 30 days of its transmittal.
optionB: It lapsed into law without the President's signature.
optionC: It was submitted to the people in a national referendum.
optionD: The Senate did not pass it before the 17th Congress ended, so it did not become law.
explanation: As of November 2026, the September 20, 2017 House approval of HB 4982 is the farthest the bill has gone. The Senate version stayed pending, and the measure died when the 17th Congress adjourned in 2019 (Rappler and GMA News, September 2017).
hint: A bill needs the approval of both chambers before it can reach the President.
whyA: It never reached the President because the Senate did not approve it.
whyB: A bill can lapse into law only after Congress passes it and sends it to the President. This one was not passed by the Senate.
whyC: Ordinary bills are not submitted to a referendum. Its fate was decided in the Senate.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang pinakamalayong naabot ng SOGIE bill ay ang approval ng House noong September 20, 2017 (HB 4982). Pero hindi ito naipasa ng Senate, kaya namatay ito pagtapos ng 17th Congress noong 2019 (Rappler at GMA News, September 2017).
hintTl: Kailangan munang aprubahan ng dalawang chamber bago makarating sa Presidente ang isang bill.

text: The SOGIESC Equality Bill, refiled in the 20th Congress in July 2025, is an anti-discrimination measure. Which act does it propose to treat as discriminatory?
optionA: Requiring all employees to undergo annual drug testing
optionB: Charging higher tuition to foreign students
optionC: Refusing to admit or expelling a student from a school because of his or her SOGIESC
optionD: Requiring government employees to wear a uniform
explanation: As of November 2026, the refiled bill lists acts such as refusing admission to or expelling a person from educational or training institutions, denying access to public health services, and refusing to recognize groups, when these are based on sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or sex characteristics (GMA News, July 2025).
hint: Look for the option where a person is treated differently because of who they are.
whyA: Drug testing rules apply to everyone and are not tied to SOGIESC.
whyB: This concerns nationality and school fees, not sexual orientation or gender identity.
whyD: A uniform rule applies to all employees and is not about SOGIESC.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, kasama sa mga discriminatory acts sa refiled bill ang pag-reject o pag-expel sa estudyante dahil sa kanyang SOGIESC, pati ang pag-deny ng health services at pag-refuse na i-recognize ang isang grupo (GMA News, July 2025).
hintTl: Hanapin yung option kung saan iba ang trato sa tao dahil sa kung sino siya.

text: In April 2026, the Philippines signed on to the Pax Silica declaration. What is Pax Silica?
optionA: A United States-led coalition of countries aiming to build secure supply chains for semiconductors and artificial intelligence technology
optionB: A China-led maritime infrastructure program under the Belt and Road Initiative
optionC: An ASEAN code of conduct on the South China Sea
optionD: A United Nations treaty banning the export of raw silica sand
explanation: As of November 2026, Pax Silica is described as a US-led strategic coalition for secure supply chains in semiconductors and AI technology. The Philippines joined in April 2026 when a trade undersecretary signed the declaration (PNA and Philstar, April 2026).
hint: 'Silica' points to silicon, the material used in computer chips.
whyB: The Belt and Road Initiative is China's program. Pax Silica is led by the United States.
whyC: The South China Sea code of conduct is a separate ASEAN-China negotiation.
whyD: It is not a UN treaty and is not about banning sand exports.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang Pax Silica ay US-led coalition para sa secure na supply chain ng semiconductors at AI technology. Sumali ang Pilipinas noong April 2026 nang pumirma ang isang trade undersecretary sa declaration (PNA at Philstar, April 2026).
hintTl: Ang 'silica' ay may kinalaman sa silicon, na gamit sa paggawa ng computer chips.

text: After the Philippines joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative in April 2026, the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) identified which site to host a planned AI industrial hub?
explanation: As of November 2026, the BCDA has earmarked about 1,600 hectares (roughly 4,000 acres) in New Clark City, Tarlac for the planned Pax Silica AI industrial hub, though the DTI has said other projects may be located elsewhere (PNA, April 2026; Manila Bulletin, August 2026).
hint: The site is a planned 'green city' in Central Luzon, inside a former US base area.
whyA: Subic is a freeport in Zambales but was not the site named for the Pax Silica AI hub.
whyB: BGC is a business district in Metro Manila, not the 4,000-acre hub site.
whyD: The Cavite Economic Zone is a PEZA zone, not the BCDA site chosen for the hub.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, nag-earmark ang BCDA ng mga 1,600 hectares (around 4,000 acres) sa New Clark City, Tarlac para sa planned Pax Silica AI hub. Sabi ng DTI, puwedeng may iba pang projects sa ibang lugar (PNA, April 2026; Manila Bulletin, August 2026).
hintTl: Planned 'green city' ito sa Central Luzon, sa dating US base area.

text: Executive Order No. 94, signed on September 11, 2025, created which body to investigate anomalies in flood control and other infrastructure projects?
explanation: As of November 2026, EO 94 (s. 2025) is the order that created the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI), a three-member ad hoc fact-finding body that prioritized flood control and other infrastructure projects from the previous ten years (EO 94, lawphil.net; Inquirer, September 2025).
hint: Its acronym has three letters and its name includes the word 'Independent'.
whyA: The Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission was an earlier body abolished in 2022. It was not created by EO 94.
whyC: No council by this name was created. EO 94 created a commission.
whyD: The PCGG was created in 1986 to recover ill-gotten wealth, not by EO 94.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang EO 94 (s. 2025) ang bumuo sa Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI). Three-member ad hoc fact-finding body ito na inuna ang flood control at iba pang infra projects sa nakaraang sampung taon (EO 94, lawphil.net; Inquirer, September 2025).
hintTl: Tatlong letra ang acronym nito, at may salitang 'Independent' sa pangalan.

text: In August 2025, Malacañang launched a website where the public could view government flood control projects on a map and report complaints or feedback. What is it called?
explanation: As of November 2026, the 'Sumbong sa Pangulo' website, launched on August 11, 2025, lists DPWH flood control projects from July 2022 onward on an interactive map and accepts public reports and feedback (PTV and ABS-CBN, August 2025).
hint: The name literally means 'report to the President' in Filipino.
whyA: 8888 is the general government complaint hotline, not the flood control project website launched in 2025.
whyB: The eFOI portal is for requesting government records under Freedom of Information.
whyC: PhilGEPS is the government procurement system where agencies post bids, not a public complaint site.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang 'Sumbong sa Pangulo' website ay inilunsad noong August 11, 2025. Makikita dito sa map ang DPWH flood control projects mula July 2022, at puwede kang mag-report o mag-feedback (PTV at ABS-CBN, August 2025).
hintTl: Literal na 'report to the President' ang ibig sabihin ng pangalan.

text: The Senate Blue Ribbon Committee and the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) both looked into flood control anomalies in 2025. Which office files the resulting criminal cases before the Sandiganbayan?
explanation: As of November 2026, flood control cases before the Sandiganbayan have been filed by the Office of the Ombudsman, starting in November 2025. Under EO 94, the ICI is only a fact-finding body that recommends cases to the Ombudsman, DOJ and other offices (EO 94, lawphil.net; Daily Tribune, September 2026).
hint: Think of the constitutional office whose prosecutors handle graft cases against public officials.
whyB: The ICI is an ad hoc fact-finding body. It recommends cases but does not file them in court.
whyC: COA audits government spending and can conduct fraud audits, but it does not prosecute cases.
whyD: The Blue Ribbon Committee holds inquiries in aid of legislation (from August 2025). It does not file criminal cases.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ang Office of the Ombudsman ang nagfa-file ng flood control cases sa Sandiganbayan, simula November 2025. Ang ICI naman ay fact-finding body lang na nagre-recommend ng cases sa Ombudsman at DOJ (EO 94, lawphil.net; Daily Tribune, September 2026).
hintTl: Isipin mo yung constitutional office na may prosecutors para sa graft cases ng mga public official.

text: The House of Representatives impeached Vice President Sara Duterte on May 11, 2026. Under Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution, which body has the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment?
explanation: As of November 2026, Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution gives the Senate the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment; the Senate convened as an impeachment court on May 18, 2026 (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net; Inquirer, May 2026).
hint: Think of the chamber that is not the one that impeaches.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa Article XI, Section 3(6) ng 1987 Constitution, ang Senate ang may sole power na mag-try at mag-decide ng lahat ng impeachment cases; nag-convene ito bilang impeachment court noong May 18, 2026.
hintTl: Isipin ang chamber na hindi siyang nag-i-impeach.
whyA: The Supreme Court can rule on whether the process followed the Constitution, but it does not try impeachment cases.
whyB: The Sandiganbayan tries graft cases against officials; impeachment is a political process tried elsewhere.
whyD: The House Committee on Justice hears complaints at the initiation stage in the House; it does not try the case.

text: On February 5, 2025, more than one-third of all the Members of the House signed a verified impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(4) of the 1987 Constitution, what is the effect of a complaint filed by at least one-third of all the Members of the House?
optionA: It must first be heard by the House Committee on Justice within 60 session days.
optionB: It must first be reviewed by the Supreme Court before it can be sent to the Senate.
optionC: It must be approved by a majority of the Senate before a trial can begin.
optionD: It constitutes the Articles of Impeachment, and trial by the Senate shall forthwith proceed.
explanation: As of November 2026, Article XI, Section 3(4) provides that a verified complaint filed by at least one-third of all the Members of the House constitutes the Articles of Impeachment, and trial by the Senate shall forthwith proceed. The February 5, 2025 complaint (215 signatories) was sent to the Senate the same day; the Supreme Court later declared those articles void under the one-year bar (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net; ABS-CBN and Manila Bulletin, February 2025).
hint: This mode skips the usual committee route.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa Article XI, Section 3(4), kapag ang verified complaint ay na-file ng at least one-third ng lahat ng Members ng House, ito na mismo ang Articles of Impeachment at magsisimula agad ang trial sa Senate. Ang complaint noong February 5, 2025 (215 signatories) ay naipadala sa Senate sa parehong araw; idineklara itong void ng Supreme Court dahil sa one-year bar.
hintTl: Nilalampasan ng mode na ito ang karaniwang dadaanan sa committee.
whyA: The committee hearing route applies to an ordinary complaint, not one already signed by one-third of the House.
whyB: The Constitution does not require Supreme Court review before transmittal to the Senate.
whyC: No Senate vote is needed to start the trial; the Senate tries the case once it receives the articles.

text: The Senate convened as an impeachment court on May 18, 2026 to try Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution, what vote is required to convict?
optionA: Concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate
optionB: Majority of the Senators present, provided there is a quorum
optionC: One-third of all the Members of the Senate
optionD: Unanimous vote of all the Senators
explanation: As of November 2026, Article XI, Section 3(6) provides that no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate. The Senate convened as an impeachment court on May 18, 2026, and the trial proper opened on July 6, 2026 (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net; The Star/Inquirer, May 2026; SunStar, July 2026).
hint: Conviction needs a much bigger share than the vote needed to impeach.
whyB: A majority of those present is not enough. The Constitution counts all the Members of the Senate.
whyC: One-third is the House threshold to impeach, not the Senate threshold to convict.
whyD: The Constitution does not require unanimity; two-thirds is enough.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa Article XI, Section 3(6), walang mako-convict kung walang concurrence ng two-thirds ng lahat ng Members ng Senate. Nag-convene ang Senate bilang impeachment court noong May 18, 2026, at nagsimula ang trial proper noong July 6, 2026 (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net).
hintTl: Mas malaking boto ang kailangan para mag-convict kaysa para mag-impeach.

text: In July 2025, the Supreme Court unanimously declared void the Articles of Impeachment transmitted to the Senate in February 2025 against Vice President Sara Duterte, and it denied the House's motion for reconsideration in January 2026. The ruling rested mainly on which constitutional rule?
optionA: The two-thirds Senate vote required for conviction
optionB: The bar against initiating impeachment proceedings against the same official more than once within one year
optionC: The rule that the Chief Justice presides when the President is on trial
optionD: The rule limiting judgment to removal and disqualification from office
explanation: As of November 2026, the Supreme Court's July 25, 2025 decision (G.R. No. 278353) held that the February 2025 articles were barred by the one-year rule in Article XI, Section 3(5), and also cited due process. The Court denied the House's motion for reconsideration on January 28, 2026 (Philstar, July 2025; GMA News and Philstar, January 2026).
hint: The rule is about timing: how often proceedings may be started against the same official.
whyA: The Senate never voted on conviction in 2025, so the two-thirds rule was not the issue.
whyC: This rule applies only when the President is on trial, which was not the case.
whyD: No judgment was rendered in 2025, so the limit on penalties was not the basis of the ruling.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, sa July 25, 2025 decision (G.R. No. 278353), sinabi ng Supreme Court na bawal ang February 2025 articles dahil sa one-year bar sa Article XI, Section 3(5), at binanggit din ang due process. Dinenay ng SC ang motion for reconsideration ng House noong January 28, 2026 (Philstar; GMA News).
hintTl: Tungkol sa timing ang rule: gaano kadalas puwedeng simulan ang proceedings laban sa iisang official.

text: After the Supreme Court declared the 2025 Articles of Impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte void, what did the Senate do with those articles on August 6, 2025?
optionA: It voted to acquit the Vice President on all articles.
optionB: It referred the articles to the Office of the Ombudsman for prosecution.
optionC: It voted to archive the articles of impeachment.
optionD: It forwarded the articles to the Supreme Court for trial.
explanation: As of November 2026, the Senate voted on August 6, 2025 to archive the 2025 articles of impeachment after the Supreme Court ruled that they were barred by the one-year rule and that the Senate had not acquired jurisdiction (GMA News, August 2025).
hint: The Senate set the articles aside instead of ruling on them.
whyA: There was no trial on the merits, so there was no vote to acquit or convict.
whyB: Impeachment articles are not prosecuted by the Ombudsman.
whyD: The Supreme Court does not try impeachment cases. Only the Senate does.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, noong August 6, 2025, bumoto ang Senate na i-archive ang 2025 articles of impeachment matapos sabihin ng SC na barred ito ng one-year rule at walang jurisdiction ang Senate (GMA News, August 2025).
hintTl: Itinabi lang ng Senate ang articles, hindi nila dinesisyunan.

text: As of November 2026, the Senate sitting as an impeachment court is hearing the case against Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(7) of the 1987 Constitution, judgment in impeachment cases shall not extend further than:
optionA: imprisonment and a fine set by the Senate
optionB: removal from office and disqualification to hold any office under the Republic
optionC: forfeiture of all properties in favor of the State
optionD: suspension from office for one year without pay
explanation: As of November 2026, Article XI, Section 3(7) limits judgment in impeachment cases to removal from office and disqualification to hold any office under the Republic; the convicted party may still be prosecuted separately under ordinary law (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net).
hint: Impeachment is a political process, so the penalty concerns public office, not jail.
whyA: Imprisonment and fines come only from regular criminal courts, not from the impeachment court.
whyC: Forfeiture is a remedy under separate laws, not a penalty the Senate can impose in impeachment.
whyD: Suspension is not an impeachment penalty. The judgment is removal and disqualification.
explanationTl: As of November 2026, ayon sa Article XI, Section 3(7), hanggang removal from office at disqualification sa anumang public office lang ang puwedeng judgment sa impeachment. Puwede pa ring kasuhan separately sa regular courts ang na-convict (1987 Constitution, lawphil.net).
hintTl: Political process ang impeachment, kaya ang parusa ay tungkol sa pwesto, hindi kulungan.
